subject: Access controls follow-up: RBAC, support access, and break-glass procedures
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@fintrust.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Access controls follow-up: RBAC, support access, and break-glass procedures

Hi Sanjay — great speaking earlier. Quick recap from our discovery and a few follow-up clarifying questions so we can align on next steps: 

Summary from call:
- FinTrust will route customer requests through a Redwood-hosted model endpoint (hosted API) for non-sensitive workloads, and a Dedicated VPC for PII-containing pipelines.
- Key concerns: RBAC/least-privilege for tenant data, support engineering access, break-glass procedures, audit logging, and retention windows for logs and data.

Follow-ups / questions:
1) PII scope: can you confirm examples of data fields you consider PII in your pipelines (e.g., SSN, account number, full legal name)?
2) Support access: what level of access is acceptable for our support/dev engineers during incident remediation (read-only vs. ephemeral elevated access)? Any existing vendor terms?
3) Break-glass: do you require pre-authorized break-glass with two-person approval and full audit trail, or would a time-limited emergency token with post-facto review suffice?
4) Retention & residency: desired retention for request/response logs and whether EU-only residency is required for any customers.

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll loop in Dev from our infra team with technical details on RBAC primitives and audit log exports.
- We’ll send a short doc summarizing our default controls + options for stricter policies (attachments).

Attached: high-level access controls overview and a SOC 2 summary.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198

Attachments: redwood-access-controls-overview.pdf, SOC2-summary.pdf
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@fintrust.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Chen <echen@fintrust.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Access controls follow-up: RBAC, support access, and break-glass procedures

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. Quick answers inline:

On PII scope:
- Primary items: SSN, bank account numbers (masked/unmasked depending on pipeline), full legal name, date of birth, and account auth tokens. We also classify any payment card details as PCI-sensitive (but those are generally handled by our payments flow).

Support access:
- Preference is strictly least-privilege. For production incidents we will allow time-limited, auditable elevated access but only via an approval flow (security lead + engineering manager). Read-only default otherwise.

Break-glass:
- We require a two-person approval for live access to unmasked PII plus automatic audit log capture of any session. Post-incident review within 48 hours. If Redwood can provide an automated approval flow + session recording/log export, that would be ideal.

Retention & residency:
- Logs containing PII must be retained for 90 days for debugging but masked in the UI. Full request/response payloads with unmasked PII should not be stored in hosted environments; those must go to the Dedicated VPC. Some EU customers will require EU-only residency (we’ll flag those accounts).

We’re targeting a vendor security review next Wednesday (31 Mar). Can you confirm if Redwood can provide:
- A short tech write-up of RBAC roles and enforcement model
- How support engineers get ephemeral access (SAML/SCIM, Just-In-Time access, or ticket-based flows)
- How break-glass approvals are recorded and exported

—Sanjay
Sanjay Rao
Head of Security, FinTrust
sanjay.rao@fintrust.com | (212) 555-0112
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@fintrust.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Access controls follow-up: RBAC, support access, and break-glass procedures

Hi Sanjay — thanks for the details. A few technical notes on how Redwood handles the items you called out (high-level; happy to expand in a tech call):

RBAC / least-privilege:
- Roles: Owner, Admin, Developer, Support, ReadOnly. Roles are tenant-scoped and enforced at the API gateway + runtime layer.
- Enforcement: policy engine applies allow/deny per endpoint and resource (models, datasets, logs).
- SCIM integration available for automated provisioning; mapping from your AD groups to Redwood roles is supported.

Support access / JIT:
- We offer JIT escalation for support via an approval workflow that integrates with your SSO (SAML/OIDC) or our internal ticketing. Escalation requests generate an auditable event with requestor, approver, and TTL.
- Elevated sessions for access to unmasked PII are time-limited (configurable, default 30 minutes) and require two approvers if AD group flag is set (matches your two-person requirement). All actions are session-recorded and logged.

Break-glass:
- We support two modes: (1) pre-authorization pairs (security + engineering manager) and (2) emergency token tied to an incident ID with mandatory post-approval. Both emit a full audit bundle (who/when/what) and session traces.

Audit logging & retention:
- Audit logs (who/what/when) are retained by default for 90 days; exports to your S3 or GCS bucket are supported for longer retention.
- Payload retention: for hosted customers we mask PII by default and purge raw content after configurable retention windows. For Dedicated VPC, raw payloads can remain customer-controlled under your retention policy.

Data residency:
- We can pin model serving and logging to region-specific clusters (US, EU). EU-only residency options available for Dedicated deployments.

Next steps I suggest:
- We’ll prepare a short (1–2 page) technical note on RBAC primitives, JIT flows, and break-glass mechanics and share it before your security review.
- If useful, we can do a 30–45 min tech deep-dive with your security and infra team before 31 Mar.

—Dev Patel
Principal Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@fintrust.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Access controls follow-up: RBAC, support access, and break-glass procedures

Thanks Sanjay — this is perfect and matches what we can support. Action items and timeline: 

- We will send the 2-page technical note on RBAC/JIT/break-glass by Tue 23 Mar EOD (Dev).
- Marissa to share SOC2 summary + access controls overview (attached) — DONE.
- Schedule a 30–45 min tech deep-dive with your security and infra team — proposed slots: Wed 24 Mar 10:00–11:00 PT or Thu 25 Mar 14:00–15:00 PT. Please confirm availability.
- For the vendor security review (31 Mar), we’ll upload the RBAC note and SOC2 artifacts to the HubSpot deal folder and grant FinTrust read access to the Drive link.

If those items look good I’ll open a HubSpot task and attach the docs. Thanks again — looking forward to the review.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198
